Name:  ___                Unit No:   ___
 
Admission Date:  ___              Discharge Date:   ___
 
Date of Birth:  ___             Sex:   M
 
Service: MEDICINE
 
Allergies: 
Gluten / Augmentin
 
Attending: ___.
 
Chief Complaint:
Fever
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
___ line
___ placement
 
History of Present Illness:
___ y/o man with a history of HTN, Refractory celiac sprue on 
home TPN (___ catheter since ___ who presents from home 
with fevers to 103 that began this AM. + Chills last night. He 
has had some cough over past few weeks productive of white 
sputum. Does report ++ Rhinorrhea, no sore throat. Also c/o some 
fatigue; denies any myalgias. He does have + sick contacts (his 
___ was out sick over past 2 weeks for the "flu"). Denies any 
N/V, abdominal pain. Does have increased BM last night after 
taking prune juice. Denies dysuria or frequency.  
.  
In ED, Temp 101.3, BP 143/63, HR 120s, 100%RA. His WBC was 20.8 
with left shift, Lactate 2.8. A U/A was negative. CXR showed no 
evidence of infiltrate. Blood cultures sent. Pt given 1 gram 
Vancomycin IV and Tylenol. He was also given 2 L IVF. Influenza 
culture sent.  

 
Past Medical History:
Refractory Celiac Disease  
Severe hypertension  
RLL pulmonary embolus - incidental finding after a CT scan was 
performed for evaluation of possible pancreatic mass. On 
coumadin x six to seven months, stopped recently.  
Cystic Pancreatic Lesions - followed with serial CT scans  
Kidney Stone - work up of this showed possible pancreatic mass  
Anxiety disorder  
Subclinical hypothyroidism  
Peripheral neuropathy  
Osteoporosis - not on a bisphosphonate  
Hypogonadism  

 
Social History:
___
Family History:
no other family members known to have celiac sprue although he 
thinks several people who died at a young age may have had it
 
Physical Exam:
Vitals: 100.9 108/48 96 16 93%RA  
GEN: thin elderly male, slightly diaphoretic  
Skin: Erythema on chest/back (per pt this is not new), warm  
HEENT: NC/AT, EOMI, PERRL, O/P clear, MMM  
Neck: No submandibular or cervical adenopathy  
Line: No erythema, no pus or tenderness at line site. No 
fluctuance.  
CV: RRR, ___ SEM  
Lungs: Crackles at the bases  
Abd: Soft, NT, mildly distended, no rebound/guarding +BS  
Ext: Venous stasis changes b/l; trace edema  
Neuro: A&O x3  

 
Pertinent Results:
___ 01:15PM URINE  COLOR-Yellow APPEAR-Clear SP ___
___ 01:15PM URINE  BLOOD-NEG NITRITE-NEG PROTEIN-NEG 
GLUCOSE-NEG KETONE-NEG BILIRUBIN-NEG UROBILNGN-NEG PH-7.0 
LEUK-NEG
___ 12:50PM   LACTATE-2.8*
___ 12:49PM   GLUCOSE-96 UREA N-23* CREAT-0.8 SODIUM-138 
POTASSIUM-3.9 CHLORIDE-102 TOTAL CO2-24 ANION GAP-16
___ 12:49PM   estGFR-Using this
___ 12:49PM   WBC-20.8* RBC-3.42*# HGB-9.0* HCT-29.2* 
MCV-86# MCH-26.3*# MCHC-30.8* RDW-17.7*
___ 12:49PM   NEUTS-89.8* LYMPHS-4.7* MONOS-5.4 EOS-0 
BASOS-0.1
___ 12:49PM   PLT COUNT-447*

ECHO
The left atrium is elongated. Left ventricular wall thickness, 
cavity size and regional/global systolic function are normal 
(LVEF >55%) Right ventricular chamber size and free wall motion 
are normal. The aortic valve leaflets (3) are mildly thickened 
but aortic stenosis is not present. No masses or vegetations are 
seen on the aortic valve. Trace aortic regurgitation is seen. 
The mitral valve leaflets are mildly thickened. There is small 
(3 x 5 mm) mobile echodensity on the posterior mitral leaflet. 
The echodensity is likely a small vegetation, although focal 
thickening of the chordal insertion is on the differential 
diagnosis. Mild (1+) mitral regurgitation is seen. The estimated 
pulmonary artery systolic pressure is normal. No vegetation/mass 
is seen on the pulmonic valve. There is no pericardial effusion. 


IMPRESSION: Probable small mitral valve vegetation.

Compared with the prior study (images reviewed) of ___, 
the mobile mitral echodensity is new. The other findings 
(including presence of mitral regurgitation) are similar. A 
tranesophageal echocardiogram would be able to better define the 
mitral valve abnormality.

Findings discussed with Dr. ___ at 1020 am on the day 
of the study.  
 
Brief Hospital Course:
#Gram Positive Sepsis/Endocarditis-Pt presented with fevers to 
103.  Blood cultures were drawn which grew out Gram Positive 
cocci in pairs/clusters and and speciated to Coag negative 
staph.  A CXR showed no evidence of infiltrate, U/A was 
negative.  It was assumed that patients infection was likely 
secondary to his indwelling Hickman line and he was started on 
Vancomycin.  ___ cultures were positive.  Repeat surveillence 
cultures showed no growth after 48 hours.  The patients Hickman 
was removed on ___ via Dr ___ in ___ (pt refused any other MD 
___ in the removal).  An Echo was subsequently done on 
___ which showed MV endocarditis.  Thus patient had  PICC 
placed (via Dr ___ as pt refused IV Nurse team) in order for 
him to receive long term antibiotics.  He was sent home to 
complete a 6 week course of Vancomycin and was to receive his 
care through an OSH with twice daily visits.
.  

#Erythema-Pt states that erythema/warmth was not new but was  
initially concerning given worry for sepsis.  However, the 
patient stated that it occured ___ calcitonin spray and was 
chronic. A common side effect of calcitonin is indeed 
flushing/erythema and thus as his fevers/WBC improved on 
vancomycin as above, there was no concern for this rash.
.  
#HTN- Given concern for septic like picture initially held all 
of the patients BP medications however his home Captopril, 
Metoprolol and Norvasc were restarted on hospital day #2.  (Pt 
refused all "hospital" medications as they could have gluten; 
thus he was given his home meds via the nurses) 
.  
#Hypothryoidism-Pt was continued on his home synthroid  
.  
#Patient Services-On admission, the patient intially refused any 
care by the housestaff.  He adamently stated he wanted his care 
only to be directed via Dr ___ Dr ___.  In addition, he 
refused any procedure unless done directly by Dr ___. (Line 
removal, PICC placement)  On numerous occasions it was explained 
to the patient and his wife that he was at a ___ hospital 
and the housestaff were an integral part of the team.  He was 
given the option of care either at an OSH vs staying here.  He 
continued to state he would like to remain at ___ however it 
was an ongoing daily discussion regarding who could help manage 
his care. 

 
Medications on Admission:
Synthroid 50mcg daily  
Omeprazole 20mg daily  
Galzin 25mg BID  
Felodipine 5mg daily  
Alprazolam 0.25mg TID: PRN  
Citracal 3 tablets daily  
Vitamin D2 50,000U q ___  
Budesonide 6mg daily  
Captopril 50mg TID  
Potassium Chloride 20mEq daily  
Vitamin B12 1500 U Qdaily  
Vitamin A  
Metoprolol 100mg BID  
Hexavitamin daily  
Azathioprine 100mg daily  
Senna PRN  

 
Discharge Medications:
1. Levothyroxine 50 mcg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO daily ().  

2. Omeprazole 20 mg Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.) Sig: One (1) 
Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.) PO daily ().  
3. Vitamin A 10,000 unit Capsule Sig: One (1) Capsule PO daily 
().  
4. Calcitonin (Salmon) 200 unit/Actuation Aerosol, Spray Sig: 
One (1)  Nasal daily ().  
5. Budesonide 3 mg Capsule, Sust. Release 24 hr Sig: One (1) 
Capsule, Sust. Release 24 hr PO DAILY (Daily).  
6. Alprazolam 0.25 mg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO TID (3 times 
a day) as needed.  
7. Potassium Chloride 20 mEq Tab Sust.Rel. Particle/Crystal Sig: 
One (1) Tab Sust.Rel. Particle/Crystal PO daily ().  
8. Citracal + D 250-200 mg-unit Tablet Sig: Three (3) Tablet PO 
daily ().  
9. Hexavitamin     Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO daily ().  
10. Galzin 25 mg Capsule Sig: One (1) Capsule PO BID (2 times a 
day).  
11. Ergocalciferol (Vitamin D2) 50,000 unit Capsule Sig: One (1) 
Capsule PO q week ().  
12. Vitamin B12-Folic Acid 0.5-1 mg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet 
PO daily ().  
13. Captopril 50 mg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO TID (3 times a 
day).  
14. Metoprolol Tartrate 100 mg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO BID 
(2 times a day).  
15. Felodipine 5 mg Tablet Sustained Release 24 hr Sig: One (1) 
Tablet Sustained Release 24 hr PO daily ().  

 
Discharge Disposition:
Home With Service
 
Facility:
___
 
Discharge Diagnosis:
Primary: 
Gram Positive Sepsis secondary to ___
Mitral Valve Endocarditis
.
Secondary
Celiac Sprue
HTN

 
Discharge Condition:
Stable

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with a high fever. You were 
found to have an infection of one of the valves of your heart.  
This may have come from the ___ line that you use for TPN. 
This line was removed and you were started on antibiotics which 
you should continue to complete for a 6 week course.  You will 
continue to get vancomycin given to you twice daily.

.
Your azathioprine was held because this medicine causes 
immunosuppression and is not felt to be good during an acute 
infection.  In addition, it was discussed that you may not 
restart this until you speak with Dr ___.
.
We have held any more TPN for now.  You will not continue TPN 
feedings until you discuss this with Dr ___
.
There were no other changes made to your medications.
.
If you have any ongoing fevers, chills, headaches, nausea, 
vomiting, abdominal pain, or swelling/redness at the line site, 
please call your doctor or return to the ER.
 
Followup Instructions:
___
